violations.policy_name: All Databases Must Use Encryption at Rest
violations.description: Encryption at rest is required for all databases in all environments to protect sensitive data from unauthorized disk access.
violations.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. Note: for most managed DB services this must be set at creation time and requires a snapshot-restore migration.

violations.policy_name: Storage Buckets Must Not Allow Public Read
violations.description: Cloud storage buckets must not have public read access enabled, preventing accidental data exposure.
violations.remediation: Set public_read_access to false and review bucket ACLs and policies. Enable Block Public Access settings where available.

violations.policy_name: Production DB Must Have At Least 2 Replicas
violations.description: Production databases must have a minimum of 2 read replicas (or multi-AZ standby instances) to ensure high availability and enable failover without data loss.
violations.remediation: Add read replicas or enable Multi-AZ. For RDS, enable Multi-AZ in the instance settings. For Aurora, add at least 2 replica instances to the cluster.

violations.policy_name: Production DB Backup Required
violations.description: All production databases must have automated backups enabled to prevent data loss in the event of failure or corruption.
violations.remediation: Enable automated backups in the database configuration. Set backup_enabled: true and configure a backup retention window.

violations.remediation: Set publicly_accessible to false and ensure the database is placed in a private subnet with security groups restricting external access.

violations.policy_name: TLS Version Must Be 1.2 or Higher
violations.description: Services must enforce a minimum TLS version of 1.2 to prevent downgrade attacks (POODLE, BEAST, etc.).
violations.remediation: Set min_tls_version to "TLSv1.2" or "TLSv1.3" in the database parameter group or server configuration.

violations.policy_name: Production DB Must Have Deletion Protection Enabled
violations.description: Production databases must have deletion protection enabled to prevent accidental deletion during infrastructure operations.
violations.remediation: Enable deletion_protection on the database. In Terraform, set deletion_protection = true. In the AWS Console, enable under Maintenance → Deletion protection.

violations.policy_name: Production DB Must Have Point-in-Time Recovery
violations.description: PITR allows recovery to any point within the backup retention window. Required for production to support recovery from application-level errors.
violations.remediation: Enable point-in-time recovery. For DynamoDB, this is a toggle in the table settings. For RDS, PITR is available when automated backups are on.

violations.policy_name: Backup Retention Must Be At Least 7 Days
violations.description: When backups are enabled, the retention period must be at least 7 days to ensure recovery from delayed-discovery incidents.
violations.remediation: Set backup_retention_days to at least 7 in the database configuration.

violations.policy_name: Compute Must Have Auto Scaling Enabled in Production
violations.description: Production compute services must have auto scaling configured to handle load spikes and maintain availability during traffic surges.
violations.remediation: Configure an Auto Scaling Group with appropriate min/max capacity and a scaling policy tied to CPU or request count metrics.

violations.policy_name: Production Compute Must Not Have Public IP
violations.description: Production compute instances should not have public IP addresses. Access should be routed through a load balancer or bastion host.
violations.remediation: Disable public IP assignment. Use a NAT gateway for outbound internet access and an Application Load Balancer for inbound traffic.

violations.policy_name: Dev Compute Must Use Cost-Optimized Instance Types
violations.description: Dev compute instances must use burstable or cost-optimized instance types to avoid unnecessary EC2 spend.
violations.remediation: Change the instance type to t3.micro, t3.small, or t3.medium. Stop and start the instance to apply the change.

violations.policy_name: Dev/Staging DB Must Use Cost-Optimized Instance Types
violations.description: Dev and staging database instances must use cost-optimized (burstable) instance types to reduce unnecessary spend on non-production workloads.
violations.remediation: Switch the instance to a cost-optimized type such as db.t3.micro, db.t3.small, or db.t3.medium. Avoid db.r5 and db.m5 classes in dev.

violations.policy_name: Databases Must Have Owner Tag
violations.description: All database services must have an 'owner' attribute to enable accountability and incident response routing.
violations.remediation: Add an 'owner' field to the database service config with the responsible team or individual's name (e.g., "platform-team", "alice@company.com").

violations.remediation: Enable versioning on the storage bucket. For S3, this is under Properties → Bucket Versioning → Enable.

violations.policy_name: Production DB Must Have Enhanced Monitoring

violations.remediation: Enable enhanced monitoring with a monitoring interval of 60 seconds or less. This requires an IAM role with CloudWatch permissions.

violations.remediation: Downsize to a t3 or t4g instance type. Reserve production-grade instance types (r5, m5) for production environments only.

violations.policy_name: Storage Must Have Lifecycle Policy Enabled
violations.description: All storage buckets must have a lifecycle policy to automatically transition or expire old data, reducing long-term storage costs.
violations.remediation: Add a lifecycle rule to transition objects older than 90 days to Glacier and expire objects older than 365 days.
